questions.q: The kinetic energy of a gas molecule is _____ temperature
options: directly proportional to square root of
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of a gas molecule is directly proportional to absolute temperature. According to kinetic theory of gases, the pressure $P$ exerted by a gas is given by $p=\frac{1}{3} \frac{M u^2}{V}$ or $p V=\frac{1}{3} M u^2$
According to gas equation $p V=R T\therefore \quad \frac{1}{3} M u^2=R T$ or $\quad \frac{1 M u^2}{3 N}=\frac{R T}{N}$ We know that $\frac{R}{N}=KK=$ Boltzmann constant or $\quad \frac{1}{2} M u^2=\frac{3}{2} K T$ But $\frac{1}{2} M u^2$ is average kinetic energy per molecule of the gas. $\therefore \quad$ Average K.E. $=\frac{3}{2} K T$ K.E. $\propto T$ Thus average kinetic energy of one mole of any gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature.

questions.solution:
In mean position,
$\begin{aligned} T & =3 m g \\ \text { Net force, } T-m g & =\frac{m v^2}{l}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & 3 m g-m g \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \frac{m v^2}{l} \\ v & =\sqrt{2 g l} \end{aligned}$
Let maximum displacement with respect to vertical is $\theta$, then $\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{2} m v^2 & =m g h \\ & =m g(l-l \cos \theta) \\ \frac{1}{2} m(2 g l) & =m g l(1-\cos \theta) \\ \cos \theta & =0 \end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \theta=90^{\circ}$

questions.q: A light ray from air is incident (as shown in figure) at one end of a glass fiber (refractive index, $\mu=1.5$ ) making an incidence angle of $60^{\circ}$ on the lateral surface, so that it undergoes a total internal reflection. How much time would it take to traverse the straight fiber of length 1 km ?
questions.solution:
Velocity of light in fiber $v=\frac{c}{\mu}=\frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5}=2 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
Straight length is 1 km , Distance covered by light, $s=\frac{1 \mathrm{~km}}{\sin 60^{\circ}}=\frac{1000}{\sqrt{3} / 2}=\frac{2000}{\sqrt{3}}$
So, time taken $=\frac{s}{v}=\frac{2000 / \sqrt{3}}{2 \times 10^8}=3.85 \mu \mathrm{~s}$

questions.solution:
At $45^{\circ}$ total internal reflection takes place so, critical angle, $C=45^{\circ}$.
Refractive index, $\mu=\frac{1}{\sin C}=\frac{1}{\sin 45^{\circ}}\begin{aligned}
& =\sqrt{2}=1.414 \\
& \approx 1.5
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If no external voltage is applied across $p-n$ junction, there would be
options: no electric field across the junction
an electric field pointing from $n$-type to p-type side across the junction
an electric field pointing from $p$-type to $n$-type side across the junction
a temporary electric field during formation of p-n junction that would subsequently disappear
questions.solution: Near the junction positive charge is built on $n$-side and negative charge on $P$-side. This sets up potential difference across the junction and internal electric field $E_i$ directed from $n$-side to $P$-side. The equilibrium is established when the field $E_i$ becomes strong enough to stop further diffusion of the majority charge carriers.

questions.q: A particle is moving in a vertical circle. The tensions in the string when passing through two positions at angles $30^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ from vertical (lowest positions) are $T_1$ and $T_2$, respectively. Then
options: tension in the string always remains the same
questions.solution:
Tension, \(\mathrm{T}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{\mathrm{r}}+\mathrm{mg} \cos \theta\)
For \(\theta=30^{\circ}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{T}_1=\frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{\mathrm{r}}+\mathrm{mg} \cos 30^{\circ} \\
& =\frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{\mathrm{r}}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \mathrm{mg}
\end{aligned}\)
For \(\theta=60^{\circ}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{T}_2=\frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{\mathrm{r}}+\mathrm{mgcos}^{60^{\circ}} \\
& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{mv}^2}{\mathrm{r}}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mg} \\
& \mathrm{~T}_1  \gt  \mathrm{T}_2
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q: When a spring is stretched by 2 cm , it stores 100 J of energy. If it is stretched further by 2 cm , the stored energy will be increased by
questions.solution:
Ist case, $\begin{aligned} U & =\frac{1}{2} k x_1^2 \\ 100 & =\frac{1}{2} k\left(2 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \\ k & =\frac{200}{4 \times 10^{-4}} \\ & =50 \times 10^4 \end{aligned}$
IInd case $\begin{aligned} U & =\frac{1}{2} k x_2^2 \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times 50 \times 10^4\left(4 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \\ & =25 \times 10^4 \times 16 \times 10^{-4} \\ & =400 \mathrm{~J} \end{aligned}$
So, stored energy increases by $400-100=300 \mathrm{~J}$
